8.h: 4 - ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿAbd ʿAwf al-Zuhrī * (ع)
8.t:
ibn ʿAbd ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Zuhrah ibn Kilāb ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy, Abū Muḥammad.
One of the Ten Promised Paradise (العشرة المبشرة), one of the six members of the Shūrā, and one of the foremost Badrīs (البدري), al-Qurashī, al-Zuhrī.
He is one of the eight who hastened to Islam.
He has a number of hadiths.
Narrating from him: ابن عباس، وابن عمر، وأنس بن مالك، وبنوه: إبراهيم، وحميد، وأبو سلمة، وعمرو، ومصعب بنو عبد الرحمن، ومالك بن أوس، وطائفة سواهم.
He has two hadiths in the two Ṣaḥīḥs (الصحيحين), and al-Bukhārī alone has five ⟦1:68⟧ hadiths from him.
The total of what he has in (Musnad Baqī): sixty-five hadiths.
In the Jāhiliyyah (الجاهلية) his name was: ʿAbd ʿAmr.
It was also said: ʿAbd al-Kaʿbah; and the Prophet ﷺ named him: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (1) .
Also narrating from him among the Companions (الصحابي): جبير بن مطعم، وجابر بن عبد الله، والمسور بن مخرمة، وعبد الله بن عامر بن ربيعة.
He came to al-Jābiyah with ʿUmar (2) , and he was in command of the right wing; and on the occasion of Sargh he was in command of the left wing.
أخبرنا محمد بن حازم بن حامد، ومحمد بن علي بن فضل، قالا:
أنبأنا أبو القاسم بن صصرى، أنبأنا أبو القاسم بن البن الأسدي (ح) .
وأنبأنا محمد بن علي السلمي، وأحمد بن عبد الرحمن الصوري، قالا:
أنبأنا أبو القاسم الحسين بن هبة الله التغلبي، أنبأنا أبو القاسم بن البن، ونصر بن أحمد السوسي، قالا:
أنبأنا علي بن محمد بن علي الفقيه، أنبأنا أبو منصور محمد، وأبو عبد الله أحمد، أنبأنا الحسين بن سهل بن الصباح ببلد (3) في ربيع الآخر، سنة سبع وعشرين وأربع مائة، قالا:
حدثنا أبو العباس أحمد بن إبراهيم بن أحمد الإمام، حدثنا علي بن حرب الطائي، حدثنا سفيان بن عيينة، عن عمرو بن دينار، سمع بجالة يقول: I was a scribe for Jazʾ ibn Muʿāwiyah, the paternal uncle of al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays, when a letter from ʿUmar came to us a year before his death: Kill every sorcerer and sorceress, and separate ⟦1:69⟧ every couple within the prohibited degrees among the Magians, and forbid them from zamzamah.
So we killed three sorceresses, and we began separating each man from his kinswoman whom he was forbidden by the Book of Allah. He prepared much food for them and invited the Magians, laid the sword across his thigh, and threw down the load of a mule or two mules of silver; and they ate without zamzamah. ʿUmar had not taken the jizyah from the Magians until ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf testified that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had taken it from the Magians of Hajar (1) .
This is a gharīb (الغريب) hadith, recorded in (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī) , (Sunan Abī Dāwūd) , (al-Nasāʾī) and (al-Tirmidhī) , by way of Sufyān, so it has reached us by a substitute route (البدل) (2) .
Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāh narrated it from ʿAmr in abridged form.
Abū Dāwūd (3) narrated the part of it on taking the jizyah from the Magians: عن الثقة، عن يحيى بن حسان، عن هشيم، عن داود بن أبي هند، عن قشير بن عمرو، عن بجالة بن عبدة، عن ابن عباس، عن ابن عوف.
أخبرنا أبو الحسن علي بن أحمد العلوي، أنبأنا محمد بن أحمد القطيعي، أنبأنا محمد بن عبيد الله المجلد (ح) .
وأنبأنا أحمد بن إسحاق الزاهد، أنبأنا أبو نصر عمر بن محمد التيمي، أنبأنا هبة الله بن أحمد الشبلي، قالا:
أنبأنا محمد بن محمد الهاشمي (4) ، أنبأنا أبو طاهر المخلص، حدثنا عبد الله البغوي، حدثنا أبو نصر التمار، حدثنا القاسم بن فضل الحداني، عن النضر بن شيبان قال:
I said to Abū Salamah: Tell me something you heard from your father, which he narrated from ⟦1:70⟧ the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He said: My father narrated to me concerning the month of Ramaḍān; he said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Allah has made (1) the month of Ramaḍān obligatory upon you, and I have instituted for you its night prayer; so whoever fasts it and stands in prayer during it out of faith and seeking reward comes out of his sins as on the day his mother bore him (2)) .
This is a sound (الحسن) gharīb (الغريب) hadith.
Recorded by: al-Nasāʾī, عن ابن راهويه، عن النضر بن شميل، and Ibn Mājah, عن يحيى بن حكيم، عن أبي داود الطيالسي، all of them from al-Ḥuddānī.
al-Nasāʾī said: What is correct is the hadith of الزهري، عن أبي سلمة، عن أبي هريرة.
أخبرنا محمد بن عبد السلام العصروني (3) ، أنبأنا عبد المعز بن محمد الهروي، أنبأنا تميم الجرجاني، أنبأنا محمد بن عبد الرحمن النيسابوري، أنبأنا محمد بن أحمد الحيري، أنبأنا أحمد بن علي الموصلي، حدثنا أبو خيثمة، حدثنا يعقوب بن إبراهيم، حدثنا أبي، عن ابن إسحاق، حدثني مكحول، عن كريب، عن ابن عباس قال: We sat with ʿUmar and he said: Have ⟦1:71⟧ you heard anything from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he commanded the Muslim man to do when he becomes forgetful in his prayer, how he should act?
I said: No, by Allah; or have you not heard anything about that from the Messenger of Allah, O Commander of the Faithful (أمير المؤمنين)?
He said: No, by Allah.
While we were thus, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf came and said: What are you two discussing?
ʿUmar said: I asked him; and he informed him.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said to him: But I have heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ give a command about that.
ʿUmar said to him: You are upright in our view; so what did you hear?
He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (If one of you becomes forgetful in his prayer so that he does not know whether he has added or omitted, then if he is in doubt between one and two, let him count it as one; and if he is in doubt between two and three, let him count it as two; and if he is in doubt between three and four, let him count it as three, so that the uncertainty falls on the side of addition; then let him prostrate twice while sitting before he gives the salām, then let him give the salām (1)) .
This is a sound (الحسن) hadith.
al-Tirmidhī graded it authentic (الصحيح), and he narrated it from: بندار (2) ، عن محمد بن خالد بن عثمة، عن إبراهيم بن سعد; so our route is higher by one degree.
And the hadith master (الحافظ) Ibn ʿAsākir narrated it at the opening of the biography of Ibn ʿAwf, and in it:
He said: Then narrate to us, for you are in our view the upright, the approved. ⟦1:72⟧
For the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, even though they are all upright, some of them are more upright than others and more firm (1) ; here ʿUmar was content with the report of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, while in the story of asking permission (2) he says: Bring someone who will testify with you.
And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib says: Whenever a man narrated to me from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I would ask him to swear an oath; and Abū Bakr narrated to me, and Abū Bakr spoke the truth (3) . So ʿAlī did not need to ask al-Ṣiddīq to swear; and Allah knows best. ⟦1:73⟧
al-Madāʾinī said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān was born ten years after the Year of the Elephant.
al-Zubayr said: al-Ḥārith ibn Zuhrah begot ʿAbd and ʿAbd Allāh, and their mother was Qaylah.
And among the offspring of ʿAbd is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿAbd ʿAwf ibn ʿAbd.
Thus did Ibn Isḥāq and Ibn Saʿd give his lineage; al-Bukhārī and al-Fasawī (1) dropped ʿAbd from his lineage, and before them ʿUrwah and al-Zuhrī said so.
al-Haytham al-Shāshī, Abū Naṣr al-Kalābādhī and others said: ʿAbd ʿAwf ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥārith ibn Zuhrah.
The mother of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān was al-Shifāʾ bint ʿAwf ibn ʿAbd ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Zuhrah.
A group said this.
Abū Aḥmad al-Ḥākim said: His mother was Ṣafiyyah bint ʿAbd Manāf ibn Zuhrah ibn Kilāb.
And it is said: al-Shifāʾ bint ʿAwf.
إبراهيم بن سعد: حدثني أبي، عن أبيه، عن عبد الرحمن بن عوف قال:
My name was ʿAbd ʿAmr; when I embraced Islam, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ named me ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (2) .
إبراهيم بن المنذر: حدثنا عبد العزيز بن أبي ثابت، عن سعيد بن زياد، ⟦1:74⟧ عن حسن بن عمر، عن سهلة بنت عاصم قالت:
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf was white, wide-eyed, with long eyelashes, aquiline-nosed, with long upper canine teeth, so that his canine sometimes made his lip bleed; he had a mass of hair falling below his ears; he was long-necked and broad-shouldered.
Ziyād al-Bakkāʾī narrated from Ibn Isḥāq, who said:
He had lost his two front teeth, being broken-toothed, left-handed and lame; he had been struck on the Day of Uḥud and his teeth were broken, and he received twenty wounds, some of them in his leg, so he became lame (1) .
الواقدي: حدثنا عبد الله بن جعفر، عن يعقوب بن عتبة، قال:
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān was a tall man, handsome of face, fine-skinned, with a slight stoop, white, tinged with redness; he did not dye his grey hair (2) .
Ibn Isḥāq said: حدثنا صالح بن إبراهيم بن عبد الرحمن بن عوف، عن أبيه، قال:
We were travelling with ʿUthmān on the road to Mecca when he saw ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, and ʿUthmān said: No one can claim any superiority over this elder in the two emigrations together.
Something similar was narrated by: العقدي، عن عبد الله بن جعفر، عن عبد الرحمن بن حميد بن عبد الرحمن، عن أبيه، عن المسور بن مخرمة، أخبرنا أبو الحسين علي بن محمد، وجماعة قالوا:
أنبأنا عبد الله بن عمر، أنبأنا أبو الوقت، أنبأنا أبو الحسن الداوودي، أنبأنا أبو محمد بن حموية، أنبأنا إبراهيم بن خزيم، حدثنا ⟦1:75⟧ عبد بن حميد (1) ، أنبأنا يحيى بن إسحاق، حدثنا عمارة بن زاذان، عن ثابت، عن أنس:
that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf: when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ emigrated, he made brotherhood between him and ʿUthmān; so it is here.
He said: I have two orchards, so choose whichever of them you wish.
He said: Rather, direct me to the market, until he said:
His wealth grew until seven hundred riding camels arrived for him carrying wheat, flour and foodstuffs; when they entered, a commotion was heard among the people of Medina. This reached ʿĀʾishah, and she said:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (ʿAbd al-Raḥmān will not enter Paradise except crawling) .
When this reached him, he said: O Mother! I call you to witness that it, with its loads and its saddle-cloths, is in the path of Allah (2) .
Recorded by: Aḥmad in his (Musnad), عن عبد الصمد بن حسان، عن عمارة.
And he said: a rejected (المنكر) hadith.
I say: In Aḥmad's wording, she said:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (I have seen ʿAbd al-Raḥmān entering Paradise crawling) .
He said: If I can, I will surely enter it standing; and he gave it, with its saddles (3) and its loads, in the path of Allah.
أخبرنا جماعة كتابة، عن أبي الفرج بن الجوزي، وأجاز لنا ابن علان وغيره، أنبأنا الكندي، قالا:
أنبأنا أبو منصور القزاز، أنبأنا أبو بكر الخطيب، أنبأنا ابن المذهب، أنبأنا القطيعي، حدثنا عبد الله بن أحمد، حدثني أبي، حدثنا هذيل بن ميمون، عن مطرح بن يزيد، عن عبيد الله بن زحر، عن علي ⟦1:76⟧ بن يزيد، عن القاسم، عن أبي أمامة، قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (I entered Paradise and heard a soft footstep, and I said: What is this?
It was said: Bilāl) .
Until he said: (I found ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf slow in coming; then he came after I had despaired.
I said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān?
He said: May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah! I did not reach you until I thought I would never see you again) .
He said: (And why was that?
He said: Because of the abundance of my wealth I was being called to account and examined (1)) .
Its chain of transmission (الإسناد) is very weak.
As for the one before it, ʿUmārah is alone in narrating it, and he is soft in hadith (لين الحديث).
Abū Ḥātim said: His hadith is written down (2) .
Ibn Maʿīn said: acceptable in hadith (صالح الحديث).
Ibn ʿAdī said: In my view, there is no harm in him (لا بأس به).
I say: He was not used as proof (يحتج به) by al-Nasāʾī.
In any case, even if ʿAbd al-Raḥmān lagged behind his companions for the reckoning and entered Paradise crawling, by way of metaphor and parable, his station in Paradise is not below the station of ⟦1:77⟧ ʿAlī and al-Zubayr (may Allah be pleased with them all).
Among his virtues: that the Prophet ﷺ testified to him of Paradise, and that he is of the people of Badr to whom it was said: (Do whatever you wish (1)) .
And he is among the people of this verse: “Allah was certainly pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree” (Qurʾān 48:18) .
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed behind him. ⟦1:78⟧
Aḥmad, in (al-Musnad): حدثنا إسماعيل، حدثنا أيوب، عن محمد، عن عمرو بن وهب الثقفي، قال:
We were with al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah, and he was asked: Has anyone of this Ummah led the Prophet ﷺ in prayer other than Abū Bakr?
He said: Yes; and he related that the Prophet ﷺ performed ablution and wiped over his leather socks and his turban, and that he prayed behind ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, and I was with him, one rakʿah of the dawn prayer, and we made up the rakʿah that had preceded us (1) .
And Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl has something similar: عن بكر بن عبد الله، عن حمزة بن المغيرة، عن أبيه (2) .
إبراهيم بن سعد: عن أبيه، عن جده that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came upon ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf while he was leading the people in prayer; ʿAbd al-Raḥmān wanted to step back, but he signalled to him: Stay in your place. So he prayed, and the Messenger of Allah prayed following the prayer of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (3) . ⟦1:79⟧
And the Imam (الإمام) Aḥmad narrated in (al-Musnad), عن الهيثم بن خارجة، عن رشدين، عن عبد الله بن الوليد:
He heard Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his father, with something similar (1) .
هشام: عن قتادة، عن الحسن، عن المغيرة بن شعبة, with the like of this.
Zurārah ibn Awfā narrated it from al-Mughīrah:
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed behind ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf.
It has also come from: خليد بن دعلج، عن الحسن، عن المغيرة.
And al-Ḥasan practises tadlīs (التدليس); he did not hear from al-Mughīrah.
عيسى بن يونس: عن عثمان بن عطاء، عن أبيه (2) ، عن ابن عمر:
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf on a raiding party, and tied the banner for him with his own hand (3) .
ʿUthmān is weak (ضعيف); but something similar was narrated by: أبو ضمرة، عن نافع بن عبد الله، عن فروة بن قيس، عن عطاء بن أبي رباح، عن ابن عمر.
Maʿmar, from Qatādah: “Those who find fault with the believers who give voluntarily” (Qurʾān 9:79) .
He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf gave half his wealth in charity, four thousand dinars.
Some of the hypocrites said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān is greatly given to showing off (4) . ⟦1:80⟧
Ibn al-Mubārak said: أنبأنا معمر، عن الزهري، قال:
In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Ibn ʿAwf gave half his wealth in charity, four thousand; then he gave forty thousand dinars in charity, and provided five hundred horses for riding in the path of Allah, then provided five hundred riding camels in the path of Allah; and most of his wealth was from trade (1) .
He recorded it in his (al-Zuhd).
سليمان بن بنت شرحبيل، أنبأنا خالد بن يزيد بن أبي مالك، عن أبيه، عن عطاء بن أبي رباح، عن إبراهيم بن عبد الرحمن بن عوف، عن أبيه:
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (O Ibn ʿAwf! You are among the rich, and you will not enter Paradise except creeping; so lend to Allah the Exalted, and He will free your feet for you) .
He said: And what shall I lend, O Messenger of Allah?
He sent to him: (Jibrīl came to me and said: Command him to host the guest, to give in times of calamity, and to feed the poor (2)) .
Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith and others said:
حدثنا محمد بن عمرو، عن أبي سلمة، عن أبيه، قال:
I saw Paradise, and that I entered it crawling, and I saw that none enters it but the poor.
I say: Its chain of transmission (الإسناد) is sound (الحسن) (3) ; it and others are dreams, and a dream has an interpretation. Ibn ʿAwf (may Allah be pleased with him) benefited from what he saw and from what reached him, until he gave away vast wealth in charity, which freed ⟦1:81⟧ his feet for him - and praise be to Allah - and he became one of the heirs of al-Firdaws; so there is no harm.
أنبأنا ابن أبي عمر، أنبأنا حنبل، أنبأنا ابن الحصين، حدثنا ابن المذهب، حدثنا أبو بكر، حدثنا عبد الله، حدثني أبي، حدثنا محمد بن عبيد، حدثنا الأعمش، عن شقيق، قال:
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān entered upon Umm Salamah and said:
O Mother of the Believers! I fear that I have perished. I am among the wealthiest of Quraysh; I sold a piece of land of mine for forty thousand dinars.
She said: My son! Spend, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (Among my companions are some who will never see me after I part from them) .
I went to ʿUmar and told him; he came to her and said: By Allah, am I one of them?
She said: By Allah, no; and I will not declare anyone free of it after you.
It was also narrated by: Aḥmad, عن أبي معاوية، عن الأعمش، فقال:
عن شقيق، عن أم سلمة (1) .
زائدة: عن عاصم، عن أبي صالح، عن أبي هريرة، قال:
There was something between Khālid and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Leave my companions to me, or my dear companions; for if one of you were to spend the like of Uḥud in gold, he would not reach the mudd of one of them, nor half of it) (2) . ⟦1:82⟧
As for al-Aʿmash, he narrated it from: أبي صالح، عن أبي سعيد الخدري (1) , and on this topic there is the hadith of زهير بن معاوية، عن حميد، عن أنس (2) .
أبو إسماعيل المؤدب: عن إسماعيل بن أبي خالد، عن الشعبي، عن ابن أبي أوفى، قال:
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf complained about Khālid to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He said: (O Khālid! Do not harm a man of the people of Badr; for if you were to spend the like of Uḥud in gold, you would not attain his deeds) .
He said: They attack me, so I answer them back.
The Prophet ﷺ said: (Do not harm Khālid, for he is one of the swords of Allah, which Allah has unleashed upon the disbelievers (3)) .
No one narrated it from al-Muʾaddib except al-Rabīʿ ibn Thaʿlab (4) ; and something similar was narrated by Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim, from al-Ḥasan, as mursal (مرسل).
شعبة: أنبأنا حصين، سمعت هلال بن يساف يحدث عن عبد الله بن ظالم المازني، عن سعيد بن زيد:
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was on Ḥirāʾ, and with him were Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, Ṭalḥah, al-Zubayr, Saʿd and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, ⟦1:83⟧ and he said: (Be firm, Ḥirāʾ! For upon you is none but a prophet, or a man of truth, or a martyr (1)) .
And Saʿīd mentioned that he was with them.
Likewise it was narrated by Jarīr, Hushaym, Abū al-Aḥwaṣ and al-Abbār, from Ḥuṣayn.
The authors of the four Sunan collections (السنن) recorded it by way of Shuʿbah, and a group likewise.
Ibn Idrīs and Wakīʿ narrated it, عن سفيان، عن منصور، عن هلال بن يساف.
Abū Dāwūd said:
It was narrated by: الأشجعي، عن سفيان، عن منصور، فقال: عن هلال (2) ، عن ابن حيان، عن عبد الله بن ظالم، عن سعيد; with corroboration (المتابعة) from Qāsim al-Jarmī, from Sufyān.
al-Tirmidhī graded it authentic (الصحيح); and it has come عن سفيان، عن منصور وحصين، عن هلال، عن سعيد himself.
أبو قلابة الرقاشي: حدثنا عمر بن أيوب، حدثنا محمد بن معن الغفاري، حدثنا مجمع بن يعقوب، عن أبيه، عن عبد الرحمن بن عبد الله بن مجمع: that ʿUmar said to Umm Kulthūm bint ʿUqbah, the wife of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf:
Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say to you: (Marry the master of the Muslims, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf?) .
She said: Yes (3) . ⟦1:84⟧
ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī said: حدثني سفيان، عن ابن أبي نجيح, that ʿUmar asked Umm Kulthūm, with something similar.
It is also narrated by two routes (1) عن عبد الرحمن بن حميد بن عبد الرحمن، عن أبيه، عن أمه أم كلثوم, with something similar (2) .
معمر: عن الزهري، حدثني عبيد الله بن عبد الله:
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave to a group among whom was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, but did not give to him, so he went out weeping.
ʿUmar met him and said: What makes you weep?
He told him, and said: I fear that he withheld from me because of some displeasure he felt toward me.
ʿUmar conveyed this to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: (Rather, I entrusted him to his faith) (3) .
قريش بن أنس: عن محمد بن عمرو، عن أبي سلمة، عن أبي هريرة:
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (The best of you are those who are best to my wives) .
So ʿAbd al-Raḥmān bequeathed to them a garden valued at four hundred thousand (4) .
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar al-Zuhrī said: Umm Bakr bint al-Miswar narrated to us that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān sold a piece of land of his to ʿUthmān for forty thousand dinars, and divided it among the poor of Banū ⟦1:85⟧ Zuhrah, the Muhājirūn, and the Mothers of the Believers.
al-Miswar said: I brought ʿĀʾishah her share, and she said: Who sent this?
I said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.
She said: Indeed, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (None will be tender toward you after me except the patient) , may Allah give Ibn ʿAwf to drink from Salsabīl of Paradise.
Recorded by: Aḥmad in his (Musnad (1)) .
علي بن ثابت الجزري: عن الوازع، عن أبي سلمة، عن عائشة، قالت:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gathered his wives during his illness and said: (Those who are patient and truthful will guard me with regard to you (2)) .
Among the best of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān's deeds was his removing himself from the matter at the time of the Shūrā, and his choosing for the Ummah the one whom the people of loosing and binding indicated; he undertook that in the most complete way, uniting the Ummah upon ʿUthmān. Had he been partial in it, he would have taken it for himself, or given it to his cousin and the closest of the group to him, Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ.
It is narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Niyār al-Aslamī (3) , from his father, who said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf was among those who gave legal opinions (الفتوى) in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, according to what he had heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. ⟦1:86⟧
Yazīd ibn Hārūn said: حدثنا أبو المعلى الجزري، عن ميمون بن مهران، عن ابن عمر: that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said to the members of the Shūrā: Would you agree that I choose for you and withdraw from it myself?
ʿAlī said: Yes, I am the first to agree, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (You are trustworthy among the people of heaven, and trustworthy among the people of earth (1)) .
Recorded by: al-Shāshī (2) in his (Musnad); and Abū al-Muʿallā (3) is weak (ضعيف).
Mujālid mentioned from al-Shaʿbī that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf led the Muslims in the Hajj in the year 13.
جويرية بن أسماء: عن مالك، عن الزهري، عن سعيد: that Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ sent a man to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān while he was standing delivering a sermon: Raise your head to the affairs of the people, meaning: call for yourself.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: May your mother be bereft of you! No one will take charge of this matter after ʿUmar except that the people will blame him (4) .
With corroboration (المتابعة) from Abū Uways ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Zuhrī.
ابن سعد: أنبأنا عبد العزيز الأويسي، حدثنا عبد الله بن جعفر، عن أم بكر، عن أبيها المسور قال:
When ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf took charge of the Shūrā, ⟦1:87⟧ the person I most loved to take it was him, and if he declined, then Saʿd. Then ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ caught up with me and said: What does your maternal uncle ʿAbd al-Raḥmān think of Allah, if he appoints someone to this matter while knowing that he himself is better than him?
I went to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and mentioned that to him, and he said: By Allah, that a knife be taken and placed at my throat, then driven through to the other side, is dearer to me than that (1) .
ابن وهب: حدثنا ابن لهيعة، عن يحيى بن سعيد، عن أبي عبيد بن عبد الله بن عبد الرحمن بن أزهر، عن أبيه، عن جده: that ʿUthmān suffered a nosebleed, so he called Ḥumrān and said:
Write the succession for ʿAbd al-Raḥmān after me.
He wrote it for him, and Ḥumrān went off to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and said: Good news!
He said: And what is that?
He said: ʿUthmān has written the succession (2) for you after him.
So he stood between the grave and the pulpit and supplicated, saying: O Allah, if this comes from ʿUthmān's appointing me to this matter, then cause me to die before him. He remained only six months before Allah took him (3) .
يعقوب بن محمد الزهري: حدثنا إبراهيم بن محمد بن عبد العزيز، عن رجل، عن طلحة بن عبد الله بن عوف، قال:
The people of Medina were dependants of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf: a third he lent his wealth, a third he paid off their debts, and a third he gave gifts to.
مبارك بن فضالة: عن علي بن زيد، عن ابن المسيب قال:
There was estrangement between Ṭalḥah and Ibn ʿAwf; then Ṭalḥah fell ill, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān came to visit him.
Ṭalḥah said: ⟦1:88⟧
You - by Allah - my brother, are better than me.
He said: Do not do that (1) , my brother!
He said: Yes indeed - by Allah - for had you fallen ill, I would not have visited you.
Ḍamrah ibn Rabīʿah, from Saʿd ibn al-Ḥasan (2) , who said:
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf could not be distinguished from among his slaves.
شعيب بن أبي (3) حمزة: عن الزهري، حدثني إبراهيم بن عبد الرحمن قال:
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf fainted during his illness (4) until they thought that his soul had departed, so that they got up from beside him and covered him; then he came to, proclaiming that Allah is greatest, and the household proclaimed that Allah is greatest. Then he said to them: Did I faint just now?
They said: Yes.
He said: You have spoken the truth! In my faint two men took me away, in whom I found harshness and roughness, and they said:
Come, we will take you to judgment before the Mighty, the Trustworthy. They took me away until they met a man.
He said: Where are you taking this one?
They said: We are taking him to judgment before the Mighty, the Trustworthy.
He said: Go back, for he is among those for whom Allah decreed happiness and forgiveness while they were in their mothers' wombs, and his sons will enjoy him for as long as Allah wills. He lived for a month after that (5) . ⟦1:89⟧
It was narrated by al-Zubaydī (1) and a group, from al-Zuhrī.
And it was narrated by Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father.
ابن لهيعة: عن أبي الأسود، عن عروة:
that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf bequeathed fifty thousand dinars in the path of Allah, and a man would be given a thousand dinars from it.
And from al-Zuhrī: that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān made a bequest to the Badrīs (البدري); they found them to be a hundred, and he gave each one of them four hundred dinars; ʿUthmān was among them, and he took it.
And with another chain of transmission (الإسناد), from al-Zuhrī: that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān bequeathed a thousand horses in the path of Allah.
قال إبراهيم بن سعد (2) : عن أبيه، عن جده:
He heard ʿAlī say on the day ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf died: Go, O Ibn ʿAwf, for you have attained its clear part and outstripped its turbid part (3) .
al-ranq: turbidity.
Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm said, from his father, who said:
I saw Saʿd at the funeral of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, in front of the bier, saying: Alas for the mountain (4) .
A group narrated it from Saʿd.
معمر: عن ثابت، عن أنس، قال:
I saw ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf: each woman among his wives was allotted a hundred thousand after his death. ⟦1:90⟧
Hishām narrated from Ibn Sīrīn, who said:
They divided among themselves their eighth (1) : three hundred and twenty thousand.
Something similar was narrated by Layth ibn Abī Muslim, from Mujāhid.
The author of (Tārīkh Dimashq) covered the reports about ʿAbd al-Raḥmān exhaustively in four quires.
When he emigrated to Medina he was poor, possessing nothing, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made brotherhood between him and Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ, one of the Nuqabāʾ. He offered to share his wealth with him equally, and to divorce for him the better of his two wives.
He said to him: May Allah bless you in your family and your wealth; but direct me to the market. So he went, and bought and sold, and made a profit; and before long he had dirhams, and he married a woman for the weight of a date stone of gold.
The Prophet ﷺ, having seen on him a trace of yellow dye, said to him: (Give a wedding feast, even if with one sheep) .
Then his affairs in trade came to what they came to (2) . ⟦1:91⟧
al-Madāʾinī, al-Haytham ibn ʿAdī (1) and a group dated his death to the year 32.
al-Madāʾinī said: He was buried in al-Baqīʿ.
Yaʿqūb ibn al-Mughīrah said: He lived 75 years (2) .
Abū ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: He was fortunate in trade; he left behind a thousand camels, three thousand sheep and a hundred horses, and he farmed at al-Jurf (3) with twenty water-carrying camels.
I say: This is the grateful rich man; and Uways is a patient poor man; and Abū Dharr, or Abū ʿUbaydah, is a chaste ascetic (الزاهد).
Ḥusayn al-Jāfī, from Jaʿfar ibn Atraqān, who said:
It reached me that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf freed thirty thousand households (4) .
